messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

This workflow should be done step-by-step so that you can iterate on your changes and any possible problems.

1. Analyze the codebase by finding and reading relevant files
2. Create a script to reproduce the issue
3. Edit the source code to resolve the issue
4. Verify your fix works by running your script again
5. Test edge cases to ensure your fix is robust
6. Submit your changes and finish your work by issuing the following command: `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT`.
   Do not combine it with any other command. <important>After this command, you cannot continue working on this task.</important>

3. You see the result(s)
4. You write your next command(s)

- Your response MUST include AT LEAST ONE bash tool call

Okay, let's see what I'm thinking here...

**Investigating Project Structure and Recent Activity**

Alright, I need to get a quick overview. My first instinct is to explore the project's layout, specifically focusing on the core directories. I'm thinking I'll start by listing the contents of `app/`, `config/`, and `db/schema.rb`. This should give me a good sense of the application's structure, configuration, and data model. I always find a quick file system scan to be the fastest way to understand a project at a glance, especially when I'm unfamiliar with it. I also want to check `docs/bots.md` because that file likely contains important details.

Then, to get a handle on recent changes and potential development patterns, I'll run `git log -n 10`. I want to see the last ten commits in the repository. This should quickly reveal any recent activity, the types of changes that have been made, and maybe even clue me in on the style of the other engineers on the project. That is the quickest way to pick up the vibe of the other developers.

# Chat Bots Design Notes

## Data Model
- Bots are modeled on `User` with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`) and `User::Bot` concern.
- `users.bot_token` (unique indexed string) stores the bot's secret authentication token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`), generated on creation when `role == "bot"`.
- `users.webhook_url` (optional string) stores the bot's HTTP webhook callback URL, normalized from blank strings to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook. Validated as an HTTP/HTTPS URL with a host (private/loopback hosts are permitted for self-hosted/local bot services).
- `users.creator_id` (foreign key to `users`) tracks who created the bot so `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` naturally grants access to administrators and the bot's creator.
- Modeling bots as `User` records allows bots to reuse:
  - `Membership` (auto-joining `Rooms::Open` on creation, toggle-based assignment on `Rooms::Closed`, `@mention` autocomplete, and unread tracking).
  - `Message#creator` (`belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User"`), displaying the bot's name and avatar in messages and web push notifications.
  - `User::Avatar` (`fresh_user_avatar_path`, uploaded avatars, and SVG initials fallback).
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate` (sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token` and `webhook_url` to `nil`, removes non-direct room memberships) so historical messages remain intact with the bot's name while immediately revoking API access and webhook delivery.
- Human-only surfaces (`AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, `Users::BansController`, `Users::SidebarsController`) scope to `User.not_bot` so bots cannot log in, be promoted/banned, or clutter account member lists.

## HTTP API (Async Posting)
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` handled by `Rooms::BotMessagesController#create`.
- Skips session authentication and CSRF forgery protection; authenticates via `User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_code])` (`active.bot.find_by(bot_token: ...)`).
- Reads `request.raw_post` (forced to UTF-8) directly as the message body so shell scripts/CI jobs can use `curl -d "..."` without JSON envelopes or form-decoding corruption. Supports `multipart/form-data` with `attachment` file uploads via `create_with_attachment!`.
- Broadcasts the message (`@message.broadcast_create`) and triggers `Room::PushMessageJob` via `Message`'s `after_create_commit` callback.

## Outgoing Webhooks (Mentions & Sync Replies)
- When a message is committed (`Message` `after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }`), `Room#deliver_webhooks_later` enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per mentioned active bot in the room that has a `webhook_url` (excluding the message creator to avoid self-loops).
- `Bot::Webhook` posts `Content-Type: application/json` to `bot.webhook_url` asynchronously in the job so message posting is never slowed down.
- `message.body.text` strips only the target bot's own `<action-text-attachment>` mention node(s) via `Message#plain_text_without_mention(bot)` while preserving other mentions and `message.body.html` keeps the full rich-text HTML.
- `room.reply_to` provides the bot's relative posting path (`/rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages`) and `message.link` provides `/rooms/:room_id/@:message_id`.
- A `200` response with `Content-Type: text/plain` or `text/html` (and non-blank body) posts a reply message into the room as the bot and calls `broadcast_create`. `204` (or non-200/unsupported content type) posts nothing.

# Chat Bots Design Notes

## Data Model
- Bots are modeled on `User` with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`) and `User::Bot` concern.
- `users.bot_token` (unique indexed string) stores the bot's secret authentication token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`), generated on creation when `role == "bot"`.
- `users.webhook_url` (optional string) stores the bot's HTTP webhook callback URL, normalized from blank strings to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook. Validated as an HTTP/HTTPS URL with a host (private/loopback hosts are permitted for self-hosted/local bot services).
- `users.creator_id` (foreign key to `users`) tracks who created the bot so `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` naturally grants access to administrators and the bot's creator.
- Modeling bots as `User` records allows bots to reuse:
  - `Membership` (auto-joining `Rooms::Open` on creation, toggle-based assignment on `Rooms::Closed`, `@mention` autocomplete, and unread tracking).
  - `Message#creator` (`belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User"`), displaying the bot's name and avatar in messages and web push notifications.
  - `User::Avatar` (`fresh_user_avatar_path`, uploaded avatars, and SVG initials fallback).
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate` (sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token` and `webhook_url` to `nil`, removes non-direct room memberships) so historical messages remain intact with the bot's name while immediately revoking API access and webhook delivery.
- Human-only surfaces (`AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, `Users::BansController`, `Users::SidebarsController`) scope to `User.not_bot` so bots cannot log in, be promoted/banned, or clutter account member lists.

## HTTP API (Async Posting)
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` handled by `Rooms::BotMessagesController#create`.
- Skips session authentication and CSRF forgery protection; authenticates via `User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_code])` (`active.bot.find_by(bot_token: ...)`).
- Reads `request.raw_post` (forced to UTF-8) directly as the message body so shell scripts/CI jobs can use `curl -d "..."` without JSON envelopes or form-decoding corruption. Supports `multipart/form-data` with `attachment` file uploads via `create_with_attachment!`.
- Broadcasts the message (`@message.broadcast_create`) and triggers `Room::PushMessageJob` via `Message`'s `after_create_commit` callback.

## Outgoing Webhooks (Mentions & Sync Replies)
- When a message is committed (`Message` `after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }`), `Room#deliver_webhooks_later` enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per mentioned active bot in the room that has a `webhook_url` (excluding the message creator to avoid self-loops).
- `Bot::Webhook` posts `Content-Type: application/json` to `bot.webhook_url` asynchronously in the job so message posting is never slowed down.
- `message.body.text` strips only the target bot's own `<action-text-attachment>` mention node(s) via `Message#plain_text_without_mention(bot)` while preserving other mentions and `message.body.html` keeps the full rich-text HTML.
- `room.reply_to` provides the bot's relative posting path (`/rooms/:room_id/:bot_token/messages`) and `message.link` provides `/rooms/:room_id/@:message_id`.
- A `200` response with `Content-Type: text/plain` or `text/html` (and non-blank body) posts a reply message into the room as the bot and calls `broadcast_create`. `204` (or non-200/unsupported content type) posts nothing.

Okay, here's my take on those thoughts, tailored for an expert audience:

**Analyzing Application Code Composition**

Alright, that `docs/bots.md` document is a goldmine. It's time to dig into the application code itself and get a solid visual of its architecture, specifically for those components relevant to my interests. I need a clear inventory of the relevant files. So, the goal is a complete picture of the application's Ruby, ERB, and JavaScript codebase located within the `app/` directory. However, to avoid visual clutter and focus on core logic, I'm going to exclude asset-related folders like `assets`, `images`, and `sounds`. It's all about getting a structured understanding of the Ruby-based backend, template rendering, and client-side interactions in their essence.

Okay, the tests ran without a hitch – that's a good starting point. Now it's time to dive deep into the code and get a real feel for the architecture. Given the domain, I'm expecting a focus on user management, rooms, and integrations – likely bots. I'll need to understand how these pieces fit together.

I'll start by reading the essential files in detail:

*   **Database Schema:** `db/schema.rb`. This will give me a solid understanding of the data structure, including the relationships between tables.
*   **Core Models:** `app/models/user.rb`, `app/models/user/bot.rb`, `app/models/user/role.rb`. I need to fully understand how users are modeled. I'll need to figure out what type of user's exist (bots) and how those are managed.
*   **Room Structure:** `app/models/room.rb`, `app/models/rooms/open.rb`, `app/models/rooms/closed.rb`, `app/models/rooms/direct.rb`. The room types are really important; each kind of room likely has its own unique behavior.
*   **Membership:** `app/models/membership.rb`, `app/models/membership/connectable.rb`. Understanding how users connect to, and interact with rooms will be a key piece.
*   **Bot Integrations:** `app/models/bot/webhook.rb`, `app/jobs/bot/webhook_job.rb`. These will define the interactions with external services, so I need to know how these are setup and managed.
*   **Controllers:** The controllers are my next target; I need to follow the interaction points.
    *   `app/controllers/bots_controller.rb`
    *   `app/controllers/rooms/opens_controller.rb`, `app/controllers/rooms/closeds_controller.rb`, `app/controllers/rooms/directs_controller.rb`
    *   `app/controllers/rooms/bot_messages_controller.rb`
    *   `app/controllers/users_controller.rb`
*   **Views:** I'll also check out a representative sample of the views: `app/views/bots/*`, `app/views/rooms/opens/*`, `app/views/rooms/closeds/*`, `app/views/rooms/layouts/*`. Layouts are always interesting.
*   **Routing:** `config/routes.rb`. This will map the requests to the controllers.
*   **Styling:** I'll glance at `app/assets/stylesheets/*` to get a sense of the styling, specifically for anything relating to switch styling.
*   **Tests:** Finally, I'll review existing bot and room tests to understand how the critical functionalities are tested.

My initial focus will be on getting a solid grasp of the models and the database schema. With a good understanding of the data structure and how it relates to user roles, room types, and bot integrations, I'll be in a better position to move on to other areas of the application and assess the overall design and functionality.

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Bot, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address, bot_token: nil, webhook_url: nil
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.insert_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end

module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_many :created_bots, -> { bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id, dependent: :nullify

    normalizes :webhook_url, with: ->(url) { url.strip.presence }

    before_validation :assign_bot_defaults, if: -> { bot? && active? }
    validates :name, presence: true, if: :bot?
    validates :bot_token, uniqueness: true, allow_nil: true
    validate :valid_webhook_url, if: -> { bot? && webhook_url.present? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def authenticate_bot(bot_code)
      return nil if bot_code.blank?

      active.bot.find_by(bot_token: bot_code)
    end
  end

  private
    def assign_bot_defaults
      self.password_digest ||= ""
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      loop do
        token = SecureRandom.base58(24)
        break token unless User.exists?(bot_token: token)
      end
    end

    def valid_webhook_url
      uri = URI.parse(webhook_url)
      unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
        errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
      end
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
    end
end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Avatar, Bannable, Bot, Mentionable, Role, Transferable

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :rooms, through: :memberships

  has_many :reachable_messages, through: :rooms, source: :messages
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :creator_id

  has_many :push_subscriptions, class_name: "Push::Subscription", dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address, bot_token: nil, webhook_url: nil
    end
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

  private
    def grant_membership_to_open_rooms
      Membership.insert_all(Rooms::Open.pluck(:id).collect { |room_id| { room_id: room_id, user_id: id } })
    end

    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def close_remote_connections(reconnect: false)
      ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: self).disconnect reconnect: reconnect
    end
end

module User::Bot
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", optional: true
    has_many :created_bots, -> { bot }, class_name: "User", foreign_key: :creator_id, dependent: :nullify

    normalizes :webhook_url, with: ->(url) { url.strip.presence }

    before_validation :assign_bot_defaults, if: -> { bot? && active? }
    validates :name, presence: true, if: :bot?
    validates :bot_token, uniqueness: true, allow_nil: true
    validate :valid_webhook_url, if: -> { bot? && webhook_url.present? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def authenticate_bot(bot_code)
      return nil if bot_code.blank?

      active.bot.find_by(bot_token: bot_code)
    end
  end

  private
    def assign_bot_defaults
      self.password_digest ||= ""
      self.bot_token ||= generate_bot_token
    end

    def generate_bot_token
      loop do
        token = SecureRandom.base58(24)
        break token unless User.exists?(bot_token: token)
      end
    end

    def valid_webhook_url
      uri = URI.parse(webhook_url)
      unless uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
        errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
      end
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      errors.add(:webhook_url, "must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL")
    end
end

class BotsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_bot, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @bots = bots_scope.with_attached_avatar.ordered
  end

  def new
    @bot = User.new(role: :bot, creator: Current.user)
  end

  def create
    @bot = User.new(bot_params.merge(role: :bot, creator: Current.user))

    if @bot.save
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    if @bot.update(bot_params)
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      render :edit, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @bot.deactivate
    redirect_to bots_url
  end

  private
    def bots_scope
      if Current.user.administrator?
        User.active.bot
      else
        Current.user.created_bots.active
      end

    end

class RoomsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ destroy ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show

  def index
    redirect_to room_url(Current.user.rooms.last)
  end

  def show
    @messages = find_messages
  end

  def destroy
    @room.destroy

    broadcast_remove_room
    redirect_to root_url
  end

  private
    def set_room
      if room = room_scope.find_by(id: params[:room_id] || params[:id])
        @room = room
      else
        redirect_to root_url, alert: "Room not found or inaccessible"
      end
    end

    # Subclasses narrow this to the room types they're allowed to act on, so that one
    # room namespace can't be used to reach another's rooms.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@room)
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_create_rooms
      if Current.account.settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators? && !Current.user.administrator?
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def find_messages
      messages = @room.messages.with_creator.with_attachment_details.with_boosts

      if show_first_message = messages.find_by(id: params[:message_id])
        @messages = messages.page_around(show_first_message)
      else
        @messages = messages.last_page
      end

class Rooms::ClosedsController < RoomsController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ show edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ update ]
  before_action :remember_last_room_visited, only: :show
  before_action :force_room_type, only: %i[ edit update ]
  before_action :ensure_permission_to_create_rooms, only: %i[ new create ]

  DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME = "New room"

  def show
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  def new
    @room  = Rooms::Closed.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Closed.create_for(room_params, users: grantees)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    selected_user_ids = @room.users.pluck(:id)
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = User.active.ordered.partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include?(user.id) }
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params
    @room.memberships.revise(granted: grantees, revoked: revokees)

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

  private
    # Allows us to edit an open room and turn it into a closed one on saving.
    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Closed)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: converting one would let its creator revise who's in it.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

    def grantees
      User.where(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def revokees
      @room.users.where.not(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def grantee_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      each_user_and_html_for(room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_prepend_to user, :rooms, target: :shared_rooms, html: html
      end
    end

    def broadcast_update_room
      each_user_and_html_for(@room) do |user, html|
        broadcast_replace_to user, :rooms, target: [ @room, :list ], html: html
      end
    end

    def each_user_and_html_for(room)
      # Optimization to avoid rendering the same partial for every user
      html = render_to_string(partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/shared", locals: { room: room })

      room.users.each { |user| yield user, html }
    end
end

class Rooms::DirectsController < RoomsController
  before_action :set_room, only: %i[ edit destroy ]
  def new
    @room = Rooms::Direct.new
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Direct.find_or_create_for(selected_users)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
  end

  private
    def selected_users
      User.where(id: selected_users_ids.including(Current.user.id))
    end

    def selected_users_ids
      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
    end

    def broadcast_create_room(room)
      room.memberships.each do |membership|
        membership.broadcast_prepend_to membership.user, :rooms, target: :direct_rooms, partial: "users/sidebars/rooms/direct"
      end
    end

    # All users in a direct room can administer it. Only direct rooms, though: this
    # relaxation is why room_scope below has to keep every other type out of reach.
    def ensure_can_administer
      true
    end

    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.directs
    end
end

My initial understanding was that in open rooms, everyone got a free pass, so the UI simply displayed a static checkmark, rendering `app/views/rooms/opens/_user.html.erb` as just a visual cue. Bots were automatically included by default.

But now, things are different for bots. They no longer *automatically* join open rooms. The goal is to give bot authors control over which rooms their bots participate in. This raises a critical question: how do we manage bot membership in *open* rooms now, particularly since people still get in automatically?

I'm thinking about this because bots get a `joined` event when added to a room, and I need to figure out the UI for users and admins to do this.

I'm starting by comparing the open room (`Rooms::Open`) situation to closed rooms (`Rooms::Closed`). In closed rooms, the UI (`rooms/closeds/_user.html.erb`) provides checkboxes (`user_ids[]`) to add/remove *any* user, humans and bots. There's even a test in `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb` that confirms this.

But how do we achieve this in *open* rooms? We have to figure out how to let someone add a bot to a specific open room, especially if the bot's "Add to all open rooms" setting is OFF. Also, if a user *does* add a bot, how do they remove it?

I'm now focusing on `app/views/rooms/opens/_form.html.erb`, `app/views/rooms/opens/_user.html.erb`, and `app/controllers/rooms/opens_controller.rb`. I've checked what the code does:
`Rooms::OpensController#new` and `Rooms::OpensController#edit` are setting `@users = User.active.ordered` and the room's data.

When creating, we have `Rooms::Open.create_for(room_params, users: Current.user)` which, importantly, calls `memberships.grant_to(User.active)` on create (or when converting from a closed room). The form, `opens/_form.html.erb`, has "Everyone" set as checked by default, so everyone has access, then it loops through `@users`. The `opens/_user.html.erb` file renders a checkmark if the current user has admin rights.

So, if bots *don't* join by default, the existing mechanism for open rooms means:
1.  People still get in automatically, checkmark and all.
2.  What about bots in an open room? That depends on whether the bot has the "Add to all open rooms" setting ON or OFF.

My train of thought now is, when creating or editing an open room, what should the form look like?! Let's look at `opens/_form.html.erb` and compare it to `closeds/_form.html.erb` again! Okay, so the initial thought is solid: adding a boolean column like `add_to_all_open_rooms` (or `auto_join_open_rooms`) to the `users` table is clean and makes for easy querying. It is smart to remember to set `add_to_all_open_rooms` to `false` on bot `deactivate` so it isn't accidentally joined to open rooms.

Now, the deeper dive begins. This is where it gets interesting.

1.  **Lifecycle Events:**
    *   **Human User Creation**: Humans are fine; they get access to open rooms as before. They don't trigger the `joined` webhook.
    *   **Bot Creation**: When `add_to_all_open_rooms` is `false`, the bot isn't added to any rooms, and `bot.rooms` is empty. If it's `true`, the bot *is* added to existing open rooms, and crucially, it *must* receive a `joined` webhook for *each* of those rooms. The webhook needs to fire even when a bot is added automatically.
    *   **Bot Update (Switch Toggle):** The logic here needs to be precise. When the switch goes from `false` to `true`, the bot joins any *new* open rooms, and it *must* receive a `joined` webhook for *only* those new rooms. If it was already in a room, we avoid a duplicate event. Likewise, when the switch goes from `true` to `false`, the bot's existing memberships are preserved, and nothing changes. And if the switch is already on, and the bot is edited, any change to the webhook URL should *not* cause a retroactive `joined` event for existing memberships.
    *   **Open Room Creation**: This is critical. When a new open room is created, *all* active humans (and any bots already selected via the form) get membership. Bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true` *must* get membership automatically and trigger the `joined` webhook. Bots that were not already in the room and have `add_to_all_open_rooms: false` only get added to the room, and get the `joined` webhook, if explicitly selected in the open room creation form.

    *   **Open Room Conversion**: When converting a closed room to open, active humans (and any bots explicitly selected), and bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true` that weren't already in the room, get membership. Again, `joined` triggers *only* for the newly added bot members.

    *   **Open Room Update**: This is essentially the same as creation and conversion – a newly checked bot with `add_to_all_open_rooms: false` gets added and receives the `joined` event. But we must be careful with edge cases around `params[:user_ids]` in controller tests.

    *   **Closed Rooms**: The logic for closed rooms mirrors open rooms (except that by default no one joins unless explicitly granted). Any bot added in the form or with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true` receives the `joined` webhook. `revise` in `memberships` is very important to avoid triggering `joined` for bots that are already members.

    *   **Direct Rooms**: Direct rooms *never* trigger `joined`, by design. This is key.

    *   **FirstRun**: No bots are involved, standard setup.

    *   **Bot Removal and Re-Addition**: The "exactly once per room" prompt phrasing is important. The test needs to cover that flow.

2.  **Implementation Considerations**: The crucial point is that `joined` events *must* be triggered *only* for new memberships – never duplicated and never for existing memberships. Careful handling of `insert_all` or other bulk insertion methods inside a transaction is required to determine the *newly* created memberships and the bots that are actually "added to the room". **Comprehensive Analysis of Bot Membership and Webhook Behavior**

Okay, here's the breakdown of my thinking after going through this. I've focused on `app/models/room.rb`, `app/jobs/bot/webhook_job.rb`, and surrounding logic, specifically looking for edge cases related to bot memberships and webhook triggers:

1.  **Bot Creation and Open Rooms:** If a bot is created with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`, it should join all existing open rooms and trigger webhooks if `webhook_url` is present. The `User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` method handles this, and also manages the updates. `after_create_commit` and `after_update_commit` callbacks ensure webhooks fire correctly on both initial creation and subsequent updates to the `add_to_all_open_rooms` flag. The logic handles scenarios where a bot is added or removed from open rooms, and where a user is being updated.

2.  **`grant_to` and `Membership.insert_all` vs. `Membership.create!`:** The key here is that `Membership.insert_all` doesn't trigger the `after_create_commit` callback on the `Membership` model, whereas `Membership.create!` does. The `grant_to` method on `Room` uses `insert_all` effectively, and ensures webhooks are triggered correctly for bots with a `webhook_url` that have been *granted* access. The `Membership.create!` method is used elsewhere, and the `after_create_commit` callback is leveraged. Both are needed, as they cover different paths that memberships can be created, and the logic in the callback covers webhooks.

3.  **Controller Actions - New and Edit (Open and Closed Rooms):**  I've paid attention to the user interface:

    *   When creating new open rooms, a new set of users are presented.
    *   In the form for creating a new room, a hidden field is included for cases where no bots are selected.
    *   In the `edit` view, I see how bots are represented, especially when a room's type is changed from Open to Closed (or vice versa). Existing members are handled well; checkboxes reflect their membership status.

4.  **Controller Actions – Update:**  The `Rooms::OpensController#update` action is where things get tricky.  It involves the key sequence of updating the room parameters and then managing bot memberships separately via `revise_bot_memberships`. By wrapping both calls in a transaction, I can ensure atomicity. This is very important.

5.  **`User#deactivate` and Bot Management:** The deactivation process in `User#deactivate` includes careful handling of `add_to_all_open_rooms`, setting it to `false`. All memberships are cleaned up.

6.  **Direct `Room` Creation:** Creating rooms directly, outside controllers, needs to be analyzed. This happens during testing or import functions.

7.  **Webhook Edge Cases:** Ensure that room names exist, so we avoid failures in the webhook job.

8.  **Security and Controller Logic:**  The controllers are securely querying using `User.active.bot` when selecting bots. The form logic is robust.

9.  **Broadcasting:** Since bots don't use ActionCable for their primary function, I can ignore broadcasts in this particular scenario.

10. **Style Guide and Conventions:**  I've checked the Ruby style guides and linting configuration to ensure code consistency. I need to run the linters and follow conventions.

**Implementation Plan Review: Auto-Joining Bots in Open Rooms**

Okay, so the linters are happy; `rubocop` and `brakeman` both report clean. Excellent. Now, before I start slinging code, I want to make sure I have a solid grip on this plan.

First up, a migration to add the `add_to_all_open_rooms` boolean column to the `users` table, defaulting to `false` and requiring it. Then, I need to run the migration for both environments - development and testing.

Next, I need to define a couple of scopes and callbacks in both `User` and `User::Bot`. The `auto_joining_open_rooms` scope, defined in both `User` and `User::Bot`, will select users with the `add_to_all_open_rooms` attribute set to `true`.  For `User::Bot`, I'll add an `after_update_commit` callback that, when the value of the `add_to_all_open_rooms` attribute changes to `true` (and the bot is active), triggers a process to grant membership to open rooms.  `User#deactivate` also requires an update to set `add_to_all_open_rooms` to `false`. When the bot is updated, it then needs to bulk insert memberships into all `Rooms::Open`, using `insert_all` to keep it performant. If it's an active bot with a webhook, I'll need to enqueue a `Bot::WebhookJob` for each newly joined room, wrapped in `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`.

In `Room`, `Rooms::Open` and `Membership`, I'll need to adjust how memberships are granted.  In `rooms/open.rb`, I'll change the `memberships.grant_to` call to use the new `auto_joining_open_rooms` scope.  In the `room.rb`'s `memberships` association, `grant_to` needs to use `insert_all`.  If it's not a direct room and something *was* inserted, I'll identify any active bots with webhooks in the inserted rows and, again, inside `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`, enqueue a `Bot::WebhookJob` for each. Finally, I'll add an `after_create_commit` callback in `Membership` that delivers the "joined" webhook for bot users. This will handle direct calls to `Membership.create!` / `room.memberships.create!` but will be skipped when `insert_all` is used in bulk insertions.

Next, I'll need to define the webhook and job behavior.  `Bot::Webhook` will now support both a "mention" and a "joined" event.  The eligible? method will check that the bot is active and has a webhook, along with other checks depending on the event. The payload will have a slightly different format depending on the event type.  The `handle_response` method, however, will be the same for both events; a successful non-blank reply will create a message as the bot.  `Bot::WebhookJob` will be responsible for dispatching between `Message` and `Room` targets to the appropriate event type.

The `BotsController` and its view will need to be updated to support the `add_to_all_open_rooms` attribute.  I need to permit this parameter in `bot_params` and add a switch to the bot form.

The `Rooms::OpensController` also needs modifications, specifically to `create`, `edit` and `update` actions.  In `create`, I'll pass in the current user and selected bots. In edit, I will pre-load the user and selected bots.  In `update`, I'll wrap the room update and bot membership revisions in a transaction. I'll need a way to determine which bots to add and remove using the `revise_bot_memberships` helper. The form also needs a hidden field and the bots should be rendered appropriately in the partial.

Finally, I'll update the documentation (`docs/bots.md`) to reflect these changes: the `add_to_all_open_rooms` design, the bot selection in open rooms, and the new "joined" webhook event.

Alright, that's the roadmap. Time to start with that database migration.

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      records = Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } }
      return if records.empty?

      inserted = Membership.insert_all(records, returning: %w[ user_id ])
      return if room.direct? || inserted.rows.empty?

      bots = User.active.bot.where(id: inserted.rows.flatten.uniq).where.not(webhook_url: nil).to_a
      return if bots.empty?

      ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit do
        bots.each { |bot| Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, room) }
      end
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    deliver_webhooks_later(message)
  end

  def open?\n    is_a?(Rooms::Open)\n  end

  def closed?\n    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)\n  end

  def direct?\n    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)\n  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

        Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, message)
      end
    end
end

class BotsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :set_bot, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]
  before_action :ensure_can_administer, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @bots = bots_scope.with_attached_avatar.ordered
  end

  def new
    @bot = User.new(role: :bot, creator: Current.user)
  end

  def create
    @bot = User.new(bot_params.merge(role: :bot, creator: Current.user))

    if @bot.save
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    if @bot.update(bot_params)
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      render :edit, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @bot.deactivate
    redirect_to bots_url
  end

  private
    def bots_scope
      if Current.user.administrator?
        User.active.bot
      else
        Current.user.created_bots.active
      end
    end

    def set_bot
      @bot = User.active.bot.find(params[:id])
    end

    def ensure_can_administer
      head :forbidden unless Current.user.can_administer?(@bot)
    end

    def bot_params
      params.require(:bot).permit(:name, :avatar, :webhook_url, :add_to_all_open_rooms)
    end
end
EOF

messages.thinking:
**Comprehensive Bot-to-Room Test Strategy**

Alright, those 14 failures are exactly what I suspected – a direct consequence of the existing test suite failing to account for bots automatically joining open rooms, plus a small issue with `message_test.rb`. This means we need to fix the existing tests *and* create a complete test suite covering every requirement and edge case for this feature.

Here's my plan, broken down by file:

1.  **`test/models/user/bot_test.rb`:** I'll start by updating the existing test for bot creation to make sure a bot, by default, *doesn't* get added to open rooms and that its `add_to_all_open_rooms` is `false` and that its `rooms` is empty. Then I'll add tests to ensure:
    *   Creating a bot *with* `add_to_all_open_rooms: true` immediately grants membership to existing open rooms (and enqueues the `joined` webhook if specified).
    *   Turning `add_to_all_open_rooms` *on* later grants membership to all existing open rooms (and only enqueues `joined` for open rooms the bot wasn't already in).

require "test_helper"

class Rooms::OpensControllerTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  setup do
    sign_in :david
  end

  test "show redirects to get general show" do
    get rooms_open_url(users(:david).rooms.opens.last)
    assert_redirected_to room_url(users(:david).rooms.opens.last)
  end

  test "new" do
    get new_rooms_open_url
    assert_response :success
  end

  test "new and edit render switches only for manual bots" do
    manual_bot = User.create!(name: "Manual Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david))
    auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

    get new_rooms_open_url
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "input[type=checkbox][name='user_ids[]'][value='#{manual_bot.id}']"
    assert_select "input[type=checkbox][name='user_ids[]'][value='#{manual_bot.id}'][checked]", count: 0
    assert_select "input[type=checkbox][name='user_ids[]'][value='#{auto_bot.id}']", count: 0

    rooms(:pets).memberships.grant_to(manual_bot)
    get edit_rooms_open_url(rooms(:pets))
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "input[type=checkbox][name='user_ids[]'][value='#{manual_bot.id}'][checked]"
    assert_select "input[type=checkbox][name='user_ids[]'][value='#{auto_bot.id}']", count: 0
  end

  test "create" do
    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts :rooms, count: 1 do
      post rooms_opens_url, params: { room: { name: "My New Room" } }
    end

    assert_equal Room.last.memberships.count, User.count
    assert_redirected_to room_url(Room.last)
  end

  test "create adds selected manual bots and auto-joining bots, not unselected manual bots" do
    selected_bot = User.create!(name: "Selected Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/selected")
    unselected_bot = User.create!(name: "Unselected Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/unselected")
    auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/auto", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    clear_enqueued_jobs

    assert_enqueued_jobs 2, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      post rooms_opens_url, params: { room: { name: "Ops" }, user_ids: [ "", selected_bot.id.to_s ] }
    end

    room = Room.last
    assert_includes room.users, selected_bot
    assert_includes room.users, auto_bot
    assert_not_includes room.users, unselected_bot
  end

  test "create forbidden by non-admin when account restricts creation to admins" do
    accounts(:signal).settings.restrict_room_creation_to_administrators = true
    accounts(:signal).save!

    sign_in :jz
    post rooms_opens_url, params: { room: { name: "My New Room" } }
    assert_response :forbidden
  end

  test "only admins or creators can update" do
    sign_in :jz

    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts :rooms, count: 0 do
      put rooms_open_url(rooms(:hq)), params: { room: { name: "New Name" } }
    end

    assert_response :forbidden
    assert rooms(:hq).reload.name, "HQ"
  end

  test "update" do
    assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts :rooms, count: 1 do
      put rooms_open_url(rooms(:pets)), params: { room: { name: "New Name" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to room_url(rooms(:pets))
    assert rooms(:pets).reload.name, "New Name"
  end

  test "update revises manual bot memberships without affecting humans or auto-joining bots" do
    manual_bot_1 = User.create!(name: "Bot One", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/one")
    manual_bot_2 = User.create!(name: "Bot Two", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/two")
    auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    pets = rooms(:pets)
    pets.memberships.grant_to(manual_bot_1)
    clear_enqueued_jobs

    # Add manual_bot_2, keep manual_bot_1 -> only manual_bot_2 gets joined webhook
    assert_enqueued_with(job: Bot::WebhookJob, args: [ manual_bot_2, pets ]) do
      assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
        put rooms_open_url(pets), params: { room: { name: pets.name }, user_ids: [ "", manual_bot_1.id.to_s, manual_bot_2.id.to_s ] }
      end
    end
    assert_includes pets.reload.users, manual_bot_1
    assert_includes pets.users, manual_bot_2
    assert_includes pets.users, auto_bot

    # Uncheck all manual bots -> removes manual bots, keeps humans and auto_bot
    assert_no_enqueued_jobs only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      put rooms_open_url(pets), params: { room: { name: pets.name }, user_ids: [ "" ] }
    end
    assert_not_includes pets.reload.users, manual_bot_1
    assert_not_includes pets.users, manual_bot_2
    assert_includes pets.users, auto_bot
    assert_includes pets.users, users(:david)
  end

  test "update a closed room to be open" do
    put rooms_open_url(rooms(:designers)), params: { room: { name: "Doesn't matter" } }
    assert_equal rooms(:designers).memberships.count, User.count
  end

  test "a direct room can't be promoted to open by its creator" do
    sign_in :kevin
    direct = rooms(:bender_and_kevin)

    put rooms_open_url(direct), params: { room: { name: "Watercooler" } }

    assert_equal "Rooms::Direct", Room.find(direct.id).type
    assert_equal [ users(:bender).id, users(:kevin).id ].sort, Room.find(direct.id).user_ids.sort
  end

  test "a direct room can't be promoted to open by an administrator either" do
    direct = rooms(:david_and_kevin)

    put rooms_open_url(direct), params: { room: { name: "Watercooler" } }

    assert_equal "Rooms::Direct", Room.find(direct.id).type
    assert_equal [ users(:david).id, users(:kevin).id ].sort, Room.find(direct.id).user_ids.sort
  end
end

The third issue, revealed in `Rooms::OpensControllerTest`, has me wondering why `put rooms_open_url(pets), params: { room: { name: pets.name }, user_ids: [ "" ] }` didn't remove `manual_bot_1` and `manual_bot_2`. I scrutinized `app/controllers/rooms/opens_controller.rb` and `app/models/room.rb`. The controller calls `revoked_bots = @room.users.bot.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: false).where.not(id: grantee_ids)`, which then calls `@room.memberships.revise(granted: selected_bots, revoked: revoked_bots)`. messages.thinking:
**Eureka! Decoding the Bug**

Okay, here's what I've figured out. We have a *major* problem in our SQL generation, let's break it down:

1.  **That `Revoked SQL` is the key!**  That `SELECT "users".* FROM "users" ... WHERE ... AND "users"."id" != NULL` is gold.  When `grantee_ids` is `[""]`, Rails is casting that empty string to `nil` for the integer `id` column. That makes the `.where.not(id: [""])` turn into `"users"."id" != NULL`. In SQL, anything compared to `NULL` using != is always `UNKNOWN`, so the `Revoked count` is 0, which is totally wrong! The fix? `params.fetch(:user_ids, []).compact_blank`! That means `[""].compact_blank` is `[]`, and that `.where.not(id: [])` generates *no* `!= NULL` filter, and we get the correct behavior by finding those manual bots.

2.  **Now, onto the second issue: Why didn't `after_update_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` fire in `User::Bot`?** Hold on, the details of the problem is: `User` and `User::Bot`. The `User` has `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, and `User::Bot` has `after_update_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms, if: -> { bot? && active? && saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?(to: true) }`. The same method name, :grant_membership_to_open_rooms! In ActiveSupport::Callbacks, registering *two* `after_commit` callbacks with the same method name overrides the first one, or replaces its `if:` condition!

Let's verify what happens by running `User._commit_callbacks` in `rails runner`. It seems we have `after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `after_update_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms`, *both* registered as a `:commit` callback with filter `:grant_membership_to_open_rooms`. So the second one is replacing the first! Or `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?` was not true inside `after_commit`. (Note: in `after_commit`, `previous_changes` is used: `add_to_all_open_rooms_previously_changed?(to: true)`, OR `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?` is cleared before `after_commit` when not inside an outer transaction)!

Also in my `rails runner` test, I ran inside `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do ... end`, so `saved_change_to_add_to_all_open_rooms?` was *still* true *before* commit! But AFTER commit (outside of the transaction), is `saved_change_to_*` replaced by `previously_changed?`? Let's check both in `rails runner`!

require "test_helper"

class Rooms::OpenTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper

  test "grants access to all human users and auto-joining bots after creation, but not default bots" do
    default_bot = User.create!(name: "Manual Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/manual")
    auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/auto", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    clear_enqueued_jobs

    room = nil
    assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
      room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "My open room with everyone!", creator: users(:david))
    end
    assert_enqueued_with(job: Bot::WebhookJob, args: [ auto_bot, room ])

    assert_equal (User.not_bot.pluck(:id) + [ auto_bot.id ]).sort, room.users.pluck(:id).sort
    assert_not_includes room.users, default_bot
  end

  test "grants access to all human users and auto-joining bots after becoming open, without duplicating existing bot memberships" do
    default_bot = User.create!(name: "Manual Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/manual")
    auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/auto", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)
    other_auto_bot = User.create!(name: "Other Auto Bot", role: :bot, creator: users(:david), webhook_url: "https://example.com/other", add_to_all_open_rooms: true)

    watercooler = rooms(:watercooler)
    watercooler.memberships.grant_to([ default_bot, auto_bot ])
    clear_enqueued_jobs

    room = watercooler.becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    assert_enqueued_with(job: Bot::WebhookJob, args: [ other_auto_bot, room ]) do
      assert_enqueued_jobs 1, only: Bot::WebhookJob do
        room.save!
      end
    end

    assert_equal (User.not_bot.pluck(:id) + [ default_bot.id, auto_bot.id, other_auto_bot.id ]).sort, watercooler.reload.users.pluck(:id).sort
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > docs/bots.md
# Chat Bots Design Notes

## Data Model
- Bots are modeled on `User` with `role: :bot` (in `User::Role`: `enum :role, %i[ member administrator bot ]`) and `User::Bot` concern.
- `users.bot_token` (unique indexed string) stores the bot's secret authentication token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`), generated on creation when `role == "bot"`.
- `users.webhook_url` (optional string) stores the bot's HTTP webhook callback URL, normalized from blank strings to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook. Validated as an HTTP/HTTPS URL with a host (private/loopback hosts are permitted for self-hosted/local bot services).
- `users.add_to_all_open_rooms` (boolean, default `false`, `null: false`) controls whether a bot automatically joins all open rooms. By default bots do not join open rooms automatically (human users still do).
- `users.creator_id` (foreign key to `users`) tracks who created the bot so `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` naturally grants access to administrators and the bot's creator.
- Modeling bots as `User` records allows bots to reuse:
  - `Membership` (toggle-based assignment on both `Rooms::Open` and `Rooms::Closed`, optional auto-joining on `Rooms::Open`, `@mention` autocomplete, and unread tracking).
  - `Message#creator` (`belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User"`), displaying the bot's name and avatar in messages and web push notifications.
  - `User::Avatar` (`fresh_user_avatar_path`, uploaded avatars, and SVG initials fallback).
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate` (sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token`, `webhook_url`, and `add_to_all_open_rooms: false`, removes non-direct room memberships) so historical messages remain intact with the bot's name while immediately revoking API access and webhook delivery.
- Human-only surfaces (`AccountsController`, `Accounts::UsersController`, `SessionsController`, `Sessions::TransfersController`, `Users::BansController`, `Users::SidebarsController`) scope to `User.not_bot` so bots cannot log in, be promoted/banned, or clutter account member lists.

## Open Room Membership Control
- `User.auto_joining_open_rooms` scopes to `not_bot.or(bot.where(add_to_all_open_rooms: true))`.
- `Rooms::Open#grant_access_to_all_users` uses `User.active.auto_joining_open_rooms`, so creating an open room or converting a closed room to open adds all active people and any bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: true`.
- Turning `add_to_all_open_rooms` on (on creation or update via `after_update_commit`) grants memberships to all existing `Rooms::Open` via `Membership.insert_all(..., returning: %w[ room_id ])`. Turning it off keeps all existing memberships.
- `Rooms::OpensController` and `rooms/opens/_user.html.erb` render checkmarks for people and auto-joining bots, and toggle switches (`user_ids[]`) for bots with `add_to_all_open_rooms: false` so admins/room creators can manually add or remove those bots in individual open rooms.

## HTTP API (Async Posting)
- `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_code/messages` handled by `Rooms::BotMessagesController#create`.
- Skips session authentication and CSRF forgery protection; authenticates via `User.authenticate_bot(params[:bot_code])` (`active.bot.find_by(bot_token: ...)`).
- Reads `request.raw_post` (forced to UTF-8) directly as the message body so shell scripts/CI jobs can use `curl -d "..."` without JSON envelopes or form-decoding corruption. Supports `multipart/form-data` with `attachment` file uploads via `create_with_attachment!`.
- Broadcasts the message (`@message.broadcast_create`) and triggers `Room::PushMessageJob` via `Message`'s `after_create_commit` callback.

## Outgoing Webhooks (Mentions, Joined & Sync Replies)
- **Mention events**: When a message is committed (`Message` `after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }`), `Room#deliver_webhooks_later` enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per mentioned active bot in the room that has a `webhook_url` (excluding the message creator to avoid self-loops).
- **Joined events**: Whenever a bot is newly added to a non-direct room (`Rooms::Open` or `Rooms::Closed`), either automatically (`add_to_all_open_rooms`) or manually (`grant_to` / `Membership.create!`), `Bot::WebhookJob` is enqueued with `(bot, room)` once per newly created membership (after transaction commit). Bulk `Membership.insert_all(..., returning: ...)` guarantees existing memberships do not trigger duplicate `joined` events. `Rooms::Direct` never triggers `joined`.
- `Bot::Webhook` posts `Content-Type: application/json` to `bot.webhook_url` asynchronously in `Bot::WebhookJob`:
  - `mention` payload includes `event`, `author`, `room`, and `message` (stripping only the target bot's mention node from `message.body.text`).
  - `joined` payload includes `event: "joined"` and `room: { id, name, reply_to }`.
- For both events, a `200` response with `Content-Type: text/plain` or `text/html` (and non-blank body) posts a reply message into the room as the bot and calls `broadcast_create`. `204` (or non-200/unsupported content type) posts nothing.
EOF
